what: The conventions Stanwood's touchweight protocols are run under: where on the key every weight is centered, the load the key weight ratio is read with, and how a wippen is weighed.

source.author: David C. Stanwood
source.doc: Standard Protocols of the New Touchweight Metrology
source.local_copy: data/references/stanwood/2000-02 - Standard Protocols of the New Touchweight Metrology.pdf

supersedes: The 1996 paper, The New Touchweight Metrology (Piano Technicians Journal, June 1996), centers the weights 13 mm in from 'the front vertical edge of the key' and reads the key weight ratio with 100 g. These protocols replace both. The setup that weighs a wippen is quoted from the 1996 paper, in the record wippen_weight, because these protocols print none: they give its definition in their glossary and no procedure, figure or photograph.

records.name: measuring_point_from_lip
records.quote: The datum point on the top of the key 13mm or 1/2" back from the front lip of the key. Weights are centered on this point when measuring Up Weight and Down Weight. When measuring Front Weight (FW) the key rests on a roller bearing on the scale pan. The point at which the front of the key rests on the bearing is directly below the Measuring Point.
records.what_for: The arm every touchweight is read on: front weight and the key weight ratio on the jig, down, up, balance and friction weight, and key friction weight.
records.which_lip: The covering's: the front edge of the keytop, which overhangs the key front (keytop_overhang in key-section.json, 2 mm). The glossary does not say which lip it means; this one is the owner's choice. Key height and key dip keep the key front as their datum.
records.engine: TouchweightProtocol::measuring_point_from_lip, which the bench can set; both shipped profiles, data/profiles/hirschkorn.json and data/profiles/measured-section.json, bind theirs to this record.

records.name: measuring_point_from_lip_imperial
records.note: The same entry's alternative, converted exactly (1 in = 25.4 mm). It stands 0.3 mm from 13 mm, 0.1 % of the arm, below the 0.1 g front weight is read to.
records.engine: The alternative the bench may be set to; the tests read it from this record.

records.name: key_weight_ratio_load
records.quote: With the scale set to zero, a 10-gram weight is placed on the back of the key, centered on a vertical axis which passes through the capstan/heel contact point. This gives results accurate to two decimal places. For instance, if the scale reads -5.5 the Key Weight Ratio (KR) would be 0.55.
records.what_for: The key weight ratio, read on the front weight jig with the scale tared: the reading over the load.
records.engine: TouchweightProtocol::key_ratio_load_g; both shipped profiles, data/profiles/hirschkorn.json and data/profiles/measured-section.json, bind theirs to this record.

records.name: wippen_weight
records.quote: The amount of weight, to the nearest 0.1 gram, of the level wippen, pivoted without friction at the wippen center, and measured at the capstan/heel contact point.

balance_weight.quote: The upward static force at the measuring point resulting from the static weight of the wippen leveraged through the key, found as: KR x WW.

records.procedure: These protocols print none: the glossary's two entries are all they give of the wippen, with no figure or photograph of its setup.

source.author: David C. Stanwood
source.note: The local copy is the author's reprint, reformatted for reading online; it keeps no page number of the journal, so its locators give the pages of the local copy.

setup.quote: The radius weight of the wippen pivoted on the wippen center, where the capstan contacts the wippen heel. The wippen heel rests on the roller at the capstan contact point. The wippen flange rests on the felt wedge so that the wippen center is aligned with the vertical axis through the center of the roller. If necessary the flange may be wedged with a sliver of wood to prevent the flange from rotating (see Photo 2).
setup.photo: Photo 2, 'A wippen on the weighing jig', page 4 of the local copy: the wippen assembly, its jack and repetition lever on it, rests by its heel on a roller bearing set on a block, and by its flange, standing upright, on a felt wedge on a second block; the wippen's long body stands horizontal.

records.which_level: The wippen's long body horizontal. The 2000 glossary says 'the level wippen' and not what is level, and the 1996 text gives the wippen no attitude in words; its Photo 2 shows the long body horizontal. This is the owner's choice, as which_lip records his for the measuring point; leveling the wippen with its center pin and the capstan's mark at one height is not it.
records.note: V covers the quotations and their locators: photo is a reading of the photograph, and which_level the owner's choice.
records.where: The roller stands under the capstan/heel contact point: the point of the heel the capstan touches, the key at rest.
